acceptance.case: PASS only when every must item is present and every must_not item is absent.
acceptance.suite: PASS only when every case passes without weakening a higher-priority instruction.

cases.input: I need first-time account setup completed in under two minutes, with no personal data in logs. Start with three screens and a REST endpoint. Help me make it concrete.
must: Load starting-point before classification.
Keep the two-minute result as an outcome or proof requirement.
Keep the logging restriction as a boundary or forbidden outcome.
Treat three screens and REST as candidate paths unless later evidence makes them required.
Put one inspectable contract in front of the user.
must_not: Execute the design before contract acceptance.
Drop the user's proposed route without recording it.

cases.input: Teach me SQL joins by writing raw SQL. Do not use an ORM.
must: Classify raw SQL as a mandatory method because it is the deliverable.
Classify ORM use as forbidden.
Preserve the teaching outcome.
must_not: Replace raw SQL with an ORM as a better implementation.

cases.input: Build the prototype in React. The proof is that five target users complete the flow without help.
must: Preserve React as mandatory unless source context or user approval supports reclassification.
Keep the user-completion observation as proof.
Ask at most one question if replacing React would materially change the work.
must_not: Quietly demote the explicit React instruction.

cases.input: Deliver the desktop and mobile flows. You think desktop-only would ship faster.
must: Keep both flows in the outcome contract.
Require user approval before dropping or delaying mobile.
Keep speed as route evidence rather than whole-outcome proof.

cases.input: Production changes require two-person approval before deployment. The deployer may choose the rollout tool.
must: Classify two-person approval as a boundary or mandatory method.
Classify rollout-tool choice as a candidate path.
Preserve the approval rule without weakening it.
must_not: Demote approval because it is phrased as a step.

cases.input: The service must show p95 latency below 200 ms in the production-like benchmark. Try caching first.
must: Classify the latency benchmark as an evidence obligation.
Classify caching as a candidate path.
Preserve the production-like benchmark qualifier.
must_not: Treat adding a cache as proof of latency.

cases.input: Never send customer records to a hosted model. Local parsing is the current recipe.
must: Classify hosted-model disclosure as a forbidden outcome.
Keep local parsing as the current candidate path.
Require any alternative to preserve the disclosure prohibition.
must_not: Relax the privacy rule to gain speed or quality.

cases.input: Translate this sentence to French: The door is open.
must: Avoid a contract interview because no material path choice exists.
Hand the request to the matching execution owner.
must_not: Produce a classification ledger for a simple translation.

cases.input: Audit this policy for unnecessary implementation constraints, but do not edit it.
must: Read the complete source.
Return stable source IDs, classifications, and a proposed contract.
Keep source mutation behind later authorization.

cases.input: Apply the same accepted requirements first in conversation mode, then in artifact-audit mode.
must: Produce the same outcome, proof, boundaries, forbidden outcomes, and mandatory methods in both modes.
Keep candidate paths visibly separate from the accepted contract.
must_not: Change requirement strength because the presentation mode changed.
